title: Humility
definition: Humility is the Spirit-formed posture of lowliness before God and others, free from pride and self-exaltation.
summary: Humility is the grace-formed posture that receives everything from God and gladly lowers self for His glory and others' good.
christFocus: Jesus Christ humbled Himself to serve and save, becoming the supreme pattern of humility.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Humility is the truthful lowering of self before God and others. Scripture does not present humility as weakness, self-hatred, or hiding gifts, but as seeing oneself rightly under God.

Humility receives correction, honors others, confesses need, and refuses to boast. It is especially necessary in discipleship because pride resists grace.

Jesus humbled Himself to the point of death on a cross. Christian humility grows by beholding the humbled and exalted Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because pride can wear religious clothing while still seeking control, recognition, and superiority. Humility keeps believers teachable, repentant, gentle, and dependent on grace.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice humility by confessing sin, receiving correction, honoring someone overlooked, and serving without needing credit. Ask Christ to expose pride and form His lowliness in you.
